metadata.source: OWASP Testing Guide v4, OWASP XSS Cheat Sheet, Public Knowledge
metadata.provenance: Synthesized from OWASP Testing Guide and public XSS knowledge, our own methodology summary

description: Cross-Site Scripting occurs when application includes untrusted data in web page without proper validation or escaping, allowing attacker to execute scripts in victim's browser.

types.description: Payload reflected immediately in response, needs victim to click link
types.testing: Inject payload in URL params, headers, check if reflected unescaped

types.description: Payload stored on server (DB, etc.) and executed when victim views page
types.example: Comment with <script>alert(1)</script> stored and shown to all users
types.testing: Inject payload in forms that store data (comments, profiles), check if executed on retrieval

types.description: Vulnerability in client-side JavaScript that processes untrusted data via DOM
types.testing: Check JS for DOM sinks like innerHTML, document.write, eval with location.hash, etc.

methodology.recon: Identify inputs: URL params, form fields, headers, cookies that are reflected or stored. Check for WAF.
methodology.hypothesis: If input reflected without encoding, possible XSS. If stored and later rendered, possible stored XSS. If JS uses DOM with user data, possible DOM XSS.
testing: Test with minimal witness: or
Try different contexts: HTML, attribute, JavaScript, URL
Try encoding bypasses: URL encode, HTML encode, case variation
Check CSP: if CSP blocks, may need bypass or report as low severity
For DOM XSS: check JS sources (location, referrer, postMessage) and sinks (innerHTML, eval, etc.)
methodology.evidence: Request with payload, response showing payload unescaped or executed, screenshot, tool output
methodology.verification: Reproduce with minimal payload, check if script executes, try bypasses for WAF, confirm not false positive (e.g., payload inside comment or encoded)
false_positive_indicators: Payload reflected but not in executable context

severity.critical: Stored XSS affecting all users, no user interaction, high impact (account takeover)
severity.high: Reflected XSS with user interaction, or stored with limited scope
severity.medium: DOM XSS requiring specific conditions, or XSS with CSP bypass needed
severity.low: XSS with strong CSP blocking, or requiring unlikely user interaction

remediation: Output encoding (HTML, attribute, JS, URL), Content Security Policy, validate input, use frameworks that auto-escape, HttpOnly cookies
report_template: Reflected XSS at {endpoint} via {param}: payload {payload} reflected unescaped, executed in browser. Repro: {steps}. Impact: {impact}. Remediation: {remediation}
